Smt. Kollamadhavi And 4 Others vs N. Amaraiah And Another
on 18 July, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Sambasiva Rao Naidu
 M.A.C.M.A.No.3889 Of 2012
Judgment :

entities.text: Kollamadhavi And 4 Others vs N. Amaraiah And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the judgment and award of the learned Special Judge for the Trial of Offences under S.Cs/S.Ts (POA)-cum-Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-XX Additional Chief Judge, at Secunderabad in O.P.No.109 of 2006, dated 12.01.2009 whereunder the learned Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Secunderabad dismissed their petition in O.P.No.109 of 2006, the appellants who are dependants of the deceased, filed the present appeal.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-XX Additional Chief Judge, at Secunderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. As could be seen from the impugned order in the present appeal, the appellants herein have filed O.P.No.109 of 2006 against respondent Nos.1 and 2 for compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- on account of the death of Kolla Yadava Reddy in a road accident.

According to the petition filed by the appellants before the Tribunal, it was their case that the appellant No.1 is wife, appellant No.2 is daughter, appellant No.3 is son and appellant Nos.4 and 5 are parents of the deceased.
The deceased was an agriculturist with Ac.5-00 of wet land and Ac.5-00 of dry land.
He was running a diary farm and supplying milk to various hotels at Siddipet and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.

On 08.03.2006 at about 12:00 noon, he along with PW2 was proceeding on a scooter bearing No.AP-36-A-2541 from Gajwel towards Hyderabad and when they reached the outskirts of Gouraram Village on Rajeev Rahadari, he dashed a tractor with trolley bearing No.AP-23-U-4374,
AP- 23-G-4375, which was left on the middle of the main road, due to some mechanical defect,
without any indications and precautions, thereby the deceased received multiple fracture injuries and while he was shifting from the accident spot to the hospital, he succumbed to injuries on the way.
The pillion rider who was examined as PW2 also received injuries.

A complaint was lodged with the concerned police who have filed final report stating that there was no negligence on the part of the tractor driver and the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased himself.

In view of the said finding, the Court below in spite of the evidence of PW2 who was present at the time of the accident and who was in fact proceeding along with the deceased as pillion rider dismissed the claim.
3. The appellants herein filed the present appeal on the following grounds:
The order of the Court below is contrary to law, facts of the case.

The Court below failed to appreciate the facts of the case in proper and prospective manner and the Tribunal grossly erred in considering that the claim application itself was filed under Section 140 of M.V.ACT and failed to grant just and reasonable compensation.
The Tribunal grossly erred in considering the evidence adduced by the appellant herein.
The Tribunal grossly erred in not believing the evidence of PW2, who was an eye witness to the accident.

The Tribunal grossly erred in holding that the appellants did Smt. Kollamadhavi And 4 Others vs N. Amaraiah And Another on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76101312/
1 not take steps to file at least scene of offence panchanama or sketch of the offence to prove the negligence on the part driver of the tractor.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal ought to have seen that the application was filed for death of bread winner of the family and ought to have considered the facts of the cased and awarded reasonable compensation.

4. Head both parties.
5.

Now the point for consideration is:
Whether the Tribunal failed to appreciate the evidence in proper way, thereby committed an error in dismissing the petition, if so, whether the appellants are entitled to receive compensation from the respondents?
6. POINT:
Learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that simply because the police filed final report alleging that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the tractor, the Tribunal ought not to have dismissed the application without considering oral evidence of PW2.
The accident occurred in a broad day light on main road.

According to the contention of the appellants, the accident spot was at a blind curve and as the tractor was left at the centre of the road, the deceased could not notice the same and dashed the vehicle.

If really the vehicle was on the extreme left side of the road, and if really the road is a straight road, as contended by the respondent, the deceased could have notice the tractor and could have averted the accident.
The circumstances spoken to by PW2 clearly indicate, that the accident occurred because of the negligence on the part of the tractor driver who left the vehicle without any indications.

Learned counsel further submitted that the Court below while commenting the evidence of PW2, came to wrong conclusion that the deceased was responsible for the accident since he was traveling with a person who is not a family member, thereby he prayed for setting aside the award.
7.
According to the evidence placed before the Court below, there is no dispute about the time of the accident.
According to the evidence of PW2, she was pillion rider of the deceased and she too suffered injuries in the accident.
PW2 deposed before the Court below that on the date of accident herself and the deceased were proceeding from Gajwel to Hyderabad with care and caution.

A tractor was left on the middle of the road due to some mechanical defect, facing towards Hyderabad in negligent manner without taking any precautions or arranging indications i.e., parking lights etc.
PW2 further deposed that the accident occurred due to the negligent conduct of the above said drier of the above said tractor.
In the cross examination PW2 has admitted that the scooter dashed the tractor from the back side.
The place of accident is National High Way.

Two buses can easily move on the road and she further deposed before the Court below that she noticed the tractor when it was at a distance of 10 yards, but she was unable to say the speed of the scooter.
She denied the suggestion that the tractor was left on the extreme left side of the road and the rider of the scooter was rash and negligent.

Learned counsel for the appellants placed reliance on judgment between National Insurance Company Limited vs Narsuri Sudarshan Rao & Others 1 and another judgment between Reliance General Insurance Compnay Limited vs Bhupathi Sujatha & Others 2 and submitted 1 2022 SCC Online TS 1107 2 2022 SCC Online AP 1318 that when the Insurance Company is not able to produce any evidence to show that there was contributory negligence on the part of the deceased, the claimants are entitled to compensation.
9.

sentences.text: As per the evidence of PW2 and other material placed by the appellants, the undisputed facts are time of the accident and death of the deceased when his scooter dashed a tractor which was left on the road.
It is true the appellants did not file any scene of offence panchanama.
Admittedly, police did not file any charge sheet but filed final report stating that there was no fault by the driver of the tractor.
They did not file any such panchanama of the scene of offence.
If the police did not prepare such panchanama, the question of appellants filing it may not arise.
10. The respondent insurance company has claimed that the accident occurred on a straight road and the tractor was parked on the left side.

In fact, the insurance company when took a plea of contributory negligence, is expected to prove its case by providing sufficient evidence to show that there was no such negligence on the part of tractor driver.
It is an admitted fact that the accident occurred when the deceased dashed a stationed tractor which is left on the road.
There is no evidence to believe that the driver of the tractor arranged some indications to know that it was parked due to some defect.
As per the cross examination of PW2 it is very clear that the accident took place on National High Way and there is sufficient place on the right side and left side of the tractor.
In such a case, it cannot be said that the tractor was parked on the extreme left side of the road.
If really the tractor was parked on the extreme left side as deposed by RW1 there is no scope for space on either side of the tractor.
RW1 is not an eye witness.
He did not state that the driver of the tractor arranged "indicator" or "signal lights" to alert the passersby about the unattended tractor.
PW2 deposed before the Court that the tractor was left at a turning and on the middle of the road.

In the light of evidence e of PW2 and RW1 that the accident took place in the day light in the after noon time, if really the tractor was on the extreme left side with some indicators the deceased could have noticed it and averted the accident.
Therefore, the above stated circumstances probablised the claim of PW2 that the deceased dashed the tractor as it was left in the middle of the road without any indicators.

11. The observations made by the Court below that the deceased drove the scooter of somebody negligently carelessly by keeping a lady who is other than his family member is without any evidence and unwarranted.
The respondent could not prove that the deceased had no driving licence.

Therefore, the death of the deceased was due to the accident which was caused due to the negligent act of the driver of the tractor on which an insurance policy was obtained, as such the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
12.
The appellants could not prove the income of the deceased on agriculture or on milk business.
However, it is clear from the evidence that the deceased was in the age group of 30-35 and being an able bodied person, he can earn at least Rs.200/- per day and Rs.6,000/- per month.
The family of the deceased consisting of 5 members the appellants and deceased himself.

Therefore,  income Smt. Kollamadhavi And 4 Others vs N. Amaraiah And Another on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76101312/
3 shall be deducted, as such his monthly contribution would be Rs.4,500/- and it was Rs.54,000/- per annum.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The age of PW1 was 24 years and the children of the deceased i.e., petitioner Nos.2 and 3 are shown as 9 years and 7 years respectively.
Therefore, the deceased can be in the age group of 30-35.
Therefore, the relevant multiplier is 16.
The appellant/claimants are entitled to receive compensation of Rs.8,64,000/-.

In addition to this amount they are also entitled to Rs.70,000/-
towards loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenditure as held by the Hon'bel Apex Court in Pranay Sethi' case.
They are entitled to receive this amount together with interest @ 7.5% per annum from both the respondents.
Out of this amount the parents of the deceased i.e., appellants Nos.4 and 5 are entitled to Rs.50,000/- each with proportionate interest.
The 1st appellant/petitioner is entitled to Rs.5,00,000/-.
The appellant Nos.2 and 3 are entitled to Rs.2,17,000/- each with proportionate interest from the date of petition till the entire amount is realized.
Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed.
13. In the result, the appeal is partly allowed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, pending Miscellaneous Applications, if any, shall stand closed.
